title: Remittances are a major household and development channel, while payment infrastructure still determines how much value reaches home
source_unit: World Bank, Cutting the cost of sending money home: Fast payment systems, digital access, and the future of remittances
geography: Global remittance flows, low- and middle-income countries, and remittance corridors

observations.period: 2024 estimate; World Bank publication dated July 2026

global_remittance_flows_2024.unit: US dollars in estimated global remittance flows in 2024

lmics_remittance_flows_2024.unit: US dollars flowing to low- and middle-income countries in 2024

average_remittance_cost.unit: approximately percent average cost of sending remittances globally in the World Bank summary

corridors_below_five_percent.unit: approximately percent of remittance corridors with average costs below 5%

observations.method: The World Bank summarizes global remittance-flow estimates and remittance-price data and connects payment costs to household support, savings, investment, small business, and development channels.
observations.uncertainty: Flows are estimates and aggregate corridor prices do not measure the fee, exchange-rate spread, speed, reliability, or access faced by every sender or recipient. The source does not establish how each transferred dollar is spent by households.
observations.subgroup: Migrant workers, diaspora households, recipients in low- and middle-income countries, remittance providers, payment platforms, small businesses, and communities dependent on cross-border transfers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Remittance costs have fallen from earlier levels and transfers can support resilience, education, housing repair, savings, investment, and enterprise. A global average can conceal low-cost corridors and substantial local access improvements.

observations.period: 2026 World Bank summary of new research on domestic fast-payment systems

denominator.unit: US-dollar remittance transaction used in the reported cost comparison

fps_cost_reduction_lower_bound.unit: percentage-point reduction in the cost of a $200 remittance associated with a domestic fast-payment system, lower bound of reported range

fps_cost_reduction_upper_bound.unit: percentage-point reduction in the cost of a $200 remittance associated with a domestic fast-payment system, upper bound of reported range

mechanism.value: Domestic fast-payment systems can reduce remittance costs primarily through competitive dynamics they unlock

observations.method: The World Bank blog summarizes research estimating the association between domestic fast-payment-system availability and the price of a $200 remittance, emphasizing competition and digital access as transmission channels.
observations.uncertainty: The reported range is a research estimate summarized in a blog post; it does not by itself prove that every corridor experiences the same reduction or that lower costs increase sending frequency, receipt, investment, or household welfare.
observations.subgroup: Senders and recipients using formal digital and domestic payment infrastructure, remittance firms, banks, mobile operators, regulators, and households with limited room for fees.
observations.counterinterpretation: Fast payments may reduce costs only where identity, accounts, network interoperability, consumer protection, connectivity, and competition are present; digital systems can also exclude people without access or create new operational risks.

boundary: This record adds a cross-border household-transfer, remittance-cost, digital-payment, and diaspora-development route. It is not respondent-level data, does not identify individual migration histories or household spending, and does not establish causal effects of fast-payment systems on welfare, migration, or political behavior.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: World Bank official blog page and linked World Bank remittance indicator page retrieved; flow totals, average costs, corridor share, and fast-payment-system estimate were cross-checked against the official blog summary.
